434.h: SAISA University of Medical Sciences and Technology is a private university and the first private university of medical sciences and technology in Sokoto State; the National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2022. Its proprietor founded it to address weaknesses he saw in existing medical institutions: weak links between medical education, research and innovation, graduates poorly prepared for work in rural communities short of qualified staff, and little connection between medical schools and primary and secondary health care.
434.a: The university specialises in the medical and health sciences and related technology.
434.c: It is located in Sokoto, Sokoto State.

436.h: Peter University is a private Catholic university jointly owned by the Catholic Dioceses of Awka and Ekwulobia, and grew out of their collaboration. It is approved by the Federal Government and licensed by the National Universities Commission, which records its establishment in 2022.
436.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes, supported by laboratories, ICT hubs and libraries.
436.c: It is located in Achina-Onneh, Anambra State.

450.h: Huda University, Gusau is a private university and the first accredited private university in Zamfara State. The National Universities Commission and the Federal Ministry of Education granted its operating approval on 15 May 2023, and its first matriculation ceremony was attended by a former Chief of Army Staff. Its name means 'guidance' in Arabic.
450.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and describes its mission as preparing students to compete globally for further study and careers.
450.c: The campus is on the Eastern Bypass, Sokoto Road, Gusau, Zamfara State.

451.h: Franco-British International University (FBIU) is a private university founded by Professor Adamu Abubakar Gwarzo, who also founded Maryam Abacha American University of Nigeria. It was established in 2023, is accredited by the National Universities Commission, and has more than 1,300 students.
451.a: FBIU combines French and British academic traditions in its teaching. Its programmes include peace and conflict studies, and it has explored clinical training and research partnerships with the National Eye Centre in Kaduna.
451.c: It is located in Kaduna, Kaduna State.

458.h: Wigwe University is a private university founded by Herbert Wigwe, co-founder and group chief executive of Access Holdings, who is credited with building Access Bank into an international bank. Its stated mission is to set a new standard for education in Africa and train the next generation of African leaders. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2023, and it held its first matriculation on 14 November 2024.
458.a: The university aims to pair internationally recruited teaching staff with curricula that are globally relevant and locally useful.
458.c: It is located in Isiokpo, in Ikwerre local government area of Rivers State, the founder's home town.

499.h: Abiola Ajimobi Technical University, formerly First Technical University, Ibadan, is a public university owned by the Oyo State Government and the first technical university in Nigeria. It was approved by the National Universities Commission in 2012 and set up to close the gap between what graduates know and what industry needs, through a mix of theory, practical work and hands-on experience. Governor Seyi Makinde renamed it in honour of his predecessor, Abiola Ajimobi.
499.a: The university has 15 programmes approved by the National Universities Commission, among them mechatronics engineering, biomedical engineering, food science and technology, cyber security, computer science, software engineering, physics with electronics, petroleum engineering, industrial chemistry and statistics.
499.c: It is located in Ibadan, Oyo State, and has on-campus student hostels.

509.h: The University of Delta (UNIDEL) is a public university owned by the Delta State Government, established by a state law on 25 February 2021. It was built on the former College of Education, Agbor, and continues that institution's long record in teacher training while expanding into wider teaching and research.
509.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate courses in faculties including agriculture, arts, education, information technology, science, engineering, medicine and law.
509.c: The university lies on the Benin-Asaba corridor, with three campuses: Agbor (Alihame), Owa-Oyibu and Owa-Alero, in Delta State.
